findings.problem: BudgetWorkflow uses separate bool fields (is_validated, is_sent) and a free-form String for status, allowing illegal state combinations such as (is_validated=false, is_sent=true, status="draft") or (is_validated=false, is_sent=false, status="sent").
findings.failure_mode: Programmer can construct or mutate a budget into an inconsistent lifecycle state that silently violates domain invariants. Callers cannot rely on type-level guarantees; invalid state propagates silently through the system.
findings.fix: Replace is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool with a single typestate enum (e.g., BudgetLifecycle: Draft, Validated, Sent) and replace status: String with the same enum or a derived Display. The constructor rejects any invalid lifecycle transition.

findings.problem: Budget id and status are raw String/primitive types instead of domain newtypes. This allows any arbitrary string as an id or status, with no type-level enforcement of format or allowed values.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid IDs or status values can enter the domain core. No compile-time guarantee that status is one of the allowed lifecycle states, leading to string-matching bugs and silent invariant violations.
findings.fix: Introduce BudgetId(newtype over String or opaque) and BudgetStatus enum with a Display impl. Replace id: String with id: BudgetId and status: String with status: BudgetStatus (or merge into lifecycle typestate).

findings.problem: mark_sent unconditionally sets status="sent" and is_sent=true without checking is_validated. Any BudgetWorkflow, including an unvalidated one, can be marked as sent.
findings.failure_mode: Unvalidated budgets can reach the sent state, bypassing the validation gate. This is a data-integrity violation: financial or operational downstream systems will process budgets that were never approved.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a fallible method or constructor on the typestate enum that requires a Validated receiver. For example: impl BudgetLifecycle { fn into_sent(self) -> Result<BudgetLifecycle, InvalidTransitionError> { ... } }

findings.problem: BudgetWorkflow exposes all fields as pub with no encapsulation. The struct itself is mutable imperative state, not inert data valid by construction.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can mutate fields directly (item.is_sent = false, item.status = "") without going through domain methods, defeating all invariants. This breaks the functional-core / imperative-shell boundary.
findings.fix: Make fields private, provide a fallible constructor that validates invariants, and expose only domain-appropriate methods. Or use the typestate enum pattern where each variant encodes allowed operations.

findings.problem: Two independent bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) encode a workflow lifecycle. This is the classic boolean-golf anti-pattern that produces N^2 state combinations with 2^N-2 illegal states.
findings.failure_mode: Every code path must remember to check both flags consistently. Missing checks produce silent bugs. The lifecycle order (validated -> sent) is not enforced by the type system.
findings.fix: Replace with a single enum: enum BudgetLifecycle { Draft, Validated, Sent }. This gives 3 valid states and 0 illegal states.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns BudgetWorkflow directly with no error type. There is no way to signal invalid transitions or precondition failures.
findings.failure_mode: On invalid input the function either silently produces wrong state or would need unwrap/panic. No fallible path for domain error handling.
findings.fix: Return Result<BudgetWorkflow, TransitionError> or redesign with typestate methods that return Result on the enum variants.

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has fundamental type-level design violations that make illegal states representable. A typestate enum replacing the bool/String lifecycle fields is required before any further implementation or verification work.
